name: NDIS Act ICT Gov Requirements
title: NDIS Act 2013 — ICT Governance Policy Requirements Register
preamble: NDIS Act 2013 — ICT Governance Policy Requirements Register
rows: The Agency's functions include: delivering the NDIS; collecting, analysing and using data and information relating to the NDIS; developing and enhancing the disability sector; facilitating innovation; building community awareness.

The ICT Governance Policy must establish a framework for enterprise data management, analytics governance, and innovation governance to support all statutory functions of the Agency. ICT capabilities must be aligned to the legislative mandate.
Align ICT capability roadmap to s.118 statutory functions; establish data analytics governance framework; require innovation management process.
Foundational section — all ICT investment should be traceable to s.118 functions.
Minister may give directions to the Agency
The Minister may give written directions to the Agency about the performance of its functions. The Agency must comply. Directions must be published in the Annual Report.

The ICT Governance Policy must establish a Ministerial direction management process ensuring that technology and data implications of Ministerial directions are assessed, implemented and tracked. Reporting obligations must be met.
Establish process for assessing ICT impact of Ministerial directions; require Board and CEO to be notified; include in ICT governance committee terms of reference.
Ministerial directions may directly affect NDIS IT systems and data.

The Board is responsible for: determining strategic objectives; ensuring the Agency performs its functions effectively; ensuring appropriate risk management; overseeing financial management; ensuring proper internal governance.

The ICT Governance Policy must establish Board-level ICT governance, including a technology risk oversight framework, an ICT investment governance process, and periodic Board reporting on ICT risk and performance.
Establish Board ICT risk reporting cadence; define technology risk appetite; require Board endorsement of ICT Strategy and major ICT investments.
Foundational governance requirement. Board must have visibility of ICT risks.
Matters to be considered in performing functions
In performing its functions, the Board must have regard to the financial sustainability of the NDIS, the objects and principles of the Act, and the interests of participants.

ICT investment decisions must be evaluated against financial sustainability, participant outcomes and the objects of the Act. The ICT Governance Policy must require cost-benefit analysis and value realisation assessment for all significant ICT projects.
Require business case process for ICT investments that demonstrates alignment to NDIS objects; embed financial sustainability analysis into project governance.
Applies to technology decisions affecting NDIS financial sustainability.
The CEO is responsible for managing the day-to-day affairs of the Agency and must act in accordance with the strategies, policies and directions of the Board.

The ICT Governance Policy must define the CEO's accountability for ICT governance, including ownership of the ICT Strategy, oversight of the CISO function, and responsibility for ensuring ICT controls are consistent with Board direction.
Define CEO ICT accountabilities; establish CEO-level review of ICT risk reports; require CEO sign-off on ICT strategic direction.
Accountability chain: Board → CEO → ICT leadership.
NDIS Rules and Regulations — ongoing ICT impact

NDIS Rules (legislative instruments) and Regulations may be made or amended at any time. They may impose new obligations on the Agency, including information-handling, record-keeping and system requirements.

The ICT Governance Policy must establish a legislative monitoring and change management process to identify and assess the ICT implications of new or amended NDIS Rules and Regulations, and update ICT controls accordingly.
Establish legislative monitoring process for NDIS Rules/Regulations; define ICT impact assessment workflow; ensure timely implementation of new obligations.
NDIS Rules are frequently updated. Continuous monitoring required.
The Agency must give information requested by Commonwealth, State or Territory Ministers relating to the NDIS or the Agency's operations.

The ICT Governance Policy must ensure that ministerial information requests can be responded to accurately and efficiently. Data governance and extract capabilities must be maintained to support ad hoc ministerial reporting.
Define ministerial information request management process; ensure data extract capabilities are available; apply data quality controls to ministerial reports.
Ministerial requests can be ad hoc; systems must be flexible.
